A craft ahead hits the upper atmosphere and blazes into a long trail of orange-white plasma, streaking down toward the surface below.
Far below, a meteor burns up in the atmosphere, a brief bright scratch of light against the dark curve of the night side.
A satellite catches the sun and flares in a brilliant point of light as it drifts slowly across the planet's face.
The orbital sunrise crests the planet's limb suddenly, a blinding arc of gold and white flooding the viewport with raw light.
A second ship passes close, its hull lit amber on one side and swallowed in shadow on the other, gone in seconds.
A booster stage separates cleanly, tumbling away in a slow spin, catching sunlight in short silver flashes as it recedes.
A comm-laser pulse sweeps past, a razor-thin thread of blue-green light vanishing almost before it registers against the black.
A piece of debris tumbles past the port side, ragged and scorched, rotating end over end in a long lazy arc.
In the far distance, a solar flare erupts from the limb of the sun, a slow silent corona of white fire.
The docking clamps engage with a deep shudder, the station filling the viewport as hull meets hull and seals with a hiss.
Another craft enters atmosphere to the south, its plasma trail a vivid violet-white ribbon curving down through the dark terminator zone.
A satellite tumbles into eclipse and vanishes, its brief glint extinguished the instant the planet's shadow swallows it whole.
A missile stage ignites and separates below, a sudden hard point of blue-white thrust burning sharp against the dark orbital plane.
Far beneath, a second meteor scratches across the atmosphere, longer and slower than expected, fading from white to deep red before dying.
The station's solar arrays catch the rising sun and blaze in a long gold flash as the approach angle shifts.
A comm-laser from the surface locks on, a single invisible beam confirmed only by the console's soft acquisition chime and indicator light.
A chunk of old hull plating drifts through the debris field ahead, edge-on and nearly invisible until it rotates and catches light.
A passing freighter fires its lateral thrusters, a brief cluster of orange jets flaring as it adjusts course and moves away.
The orbital sunrise hits the cloud tops far below first, turning them a brilliant layered rose and copper before the limb clears.
A solar flare sends a ripple of charged particles skimming past, the navigation console flickering briefly before shielding absorbs the surge.
A spent booster drifts into the upper atmosphere below and ignites, burning a slow orange arc across the dark side terminator.
Two satellites cross paths near the limb, each catching a glint in quick succession like a pair of signal lamps blinking once.
A docking arm extends from the station and locks into the approach guide rail with a precise, heavy magnetic clunk.
A debris cloud from a prior collision spreads across the orbital lane ahead, hundreds of small bright fragments scattering the sunlight into sparks.
A second ship's retro-rockets fire in a long sustained burn, pushing it into a lower arc, its exhaust plume fanning wide and pale.
